tasks.instruction: humanize.intcomma raises an overflow error for Python integers larger than the float range. Format arbitrarily large positive and negative integers with comma grouping, while preserving ordinary integer formatting.
tasks.verifier_code:
import humanize
v = 10**400 + 123
assert humanize.intcomma(v) == f'{v:,}'
assert humanize.intcomma(-v) == f'{-v:,}'
assert humanize.intcomma(1234567) == '1,234,567'

tasks.instruction: humanize.metric can show an extra significant digit when rounding carries the mantissa to the next power of ten. Keep the requested precision for values such as 9999, 99999 and 9.99999, including negative values and a custom precision. Preserve ordinary metric output.
tasks.verifier_code:
import humanize
assert humanize.metric(9999) == '10.0 k'
assert humanize.metric(99999) == '100 k'
assert humanize.metric(9.99999) == '10.0'
assert humanize.metric(-9999) == '-10.0 k'
assert humanize.metric(9.999, precision=2) == '10'
assert humanize.metric(999.4) == '999'

tasks.instruction: humanize.natural_list currently expects indexable lists. Make it accept any finite iterable, including tuples, generators, mapping key views and ranges. Preserve existing wording and stringify each item once.
tasks.verifier_code:
import humanize
assert humanize.natural_list(iter(())) == ''
assert humanize.natural_list(('one',)) == 'one'
assert humanize.natural_list(('one', 'two')) == 'one and two'
assert humanize.natural_list((x for x in ['one', 'two', 'three'])) == 'one, two and three'
assert humanize.natural_list({'one': 1, 'two': 2}.keys()) == 'one and two'
assert humanize.natural_list(range(1, 4)) == '1, 2 and 3'

tasks.instruction: humanize.intword can display a value just below the next named power as 1000.0 of the lower unit. When formatting rounds to the next named unit, carry the result to that unit. Preserve the documented gap between decillion and googol.
tasks.verifier_code:
import humanize
for power, unit in [(24, 'septillion'), (27, 'octillion'), (30, 'nonillion'), (33, 'decillion')]:
    assert humanize.intword(10**power - 1) == f'1.0 {unit}'
    assert humanize.intword(10**power - 1, '%.0f') == f'1 {unit}'
assert humanize.intword(10**36) == '1000.0 decillion'
assert humanize.intword(2 * 10**100) == '2.0 googol'

tasks.instruction: humanize.naturaldelta truncates multi-year durations instead of rounding to the nearest year when months are disabled. Format durations around 2.4, 2.6 and 2.9 years correctly; preserve exact-year and short-duration behavior.
tasks.verifier_code:
import datetime as dt
import humanize
assert humanize.naturaldelta(dt.timedelta(days=365 * 2), months=False) == '2 years'
assert humanize.naturaldelta(dt.timedelta(days=365 * 2.4), months=False) == '2 years'
assert humanize.naturaldelta(dt.timedelta(days=365 * 2.6), months=False) == '3 years'
assert humanize.naturaldelta(dt.timedelta(days=365 * 2.9), months=False) == '3 years'
assert humanize.naturaldelta(dt.timedelta(days=9), months=False) == '9 days'
